newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay to extradite Argentine "Dirty War" couple.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay to extradite Argentine "Dirty War" couple.

text.p: Paraguay will extradite a former Argentine army doctor and his wife on charges of kidnapping the children of people who "disappeared" during the late 1970s "Dirty War", a court official said Tuesday.
Former Major Norberto Atilio Bianco and his wife Susana Wehrli were arrested by Interpol in Asuncion on Monday.
The charges were first filed by the Argentine human rights group Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo in 1987, when Paraguay was under the dictatorship of Gen. Alfredo Stroessner.
"What we don't know is when they will come and get them, because Argentina's Interpol has not issued an arrest warrant yet," a court official told Reuters.

The two children involved, Carolina, now 20, and Pablo, now 21, were brought up as Bianco's own but are suspected to be the children of people killed by the Argentine military in their brutal war on suspected leftists.
Carolina and Pablo, who have both married Paraguayans, both insist the Biancos are their real parents.
"They are our true mother and father and we do not want to be separated from them," Caroline told reporters.
She said she was seeking an audition with Paraguayan President Juan Carlos Wasmosy to plead with him to intervene.
Bianco and his wife moved to Paraguay in the 1980s when the Grandmothers, a group made up of relatives of the tens of thousands who "disappeared", began legal action.

The Biancos are charged with forging documents and misappropriating minors. Their lawyer, Gilda Burgstaller, said she was optimistic because "there is not one single relative who claims paternity of the children."
